evidence_summary: Effects Database documents the Applied FW-3 as U.S.-made by Applied Audio and lists the major marketed variants under Guild, Crown, Kadent, Jax-USA, Atlantic, Lou Rose, Magnum, Nomad and V-Jay.
Guild FW-3 is explicitly documented as an Applied-built U.S. OEM state; retain Guild as marketed identity rather than builder.
Crown FW-3 is documented as part of the Applied FW-3 OEM family.
Kadent FW-3 is documented as U.S.-produced by Applied Audio and shares the Applied FW-3 platform.
Lou Rose FW-3 is explicitly documented as manufactured by Applied Audio in the U.S. and distributed through Lou Rose Music.
V-Jay FW-3 is documented as U.S.-made by Applied Audio and listed as a marketed variant of the Applied FW-3.
The Applied FW-3 family index links Hohner FW-10 Dirty Wah'er to the Applied FW-3 OEM line; retain the Hohner identity separately.

Tone Machines documents Applied Audio's 1977 Hohner ME-30 as a U.S. reintroduction of the Shin-Ei ME-7-derived Surf/Siren family; this is an OEM relationship, not a Shin-Ei physical-build attribution.
Hohner's MF-50 is documented within the Shin-Ei Companion FY-6 ecosystem and predates Hohner's later Applied Audio-built Sound Modifier lineup.
Tone Machines documents Hohner's later Sound Modifier connection with Applied Audio and identifies the Tri-Dirty Booster within that Applied-built lineup.
Applied's FW-3 and wah OEM index associates Hohner FW-10 and WW-20 with the Applied product family; retain model-specific sourcing before treating every Hohner wah variant as the same build state.
